title: YY1 mutations disrupt corticogenesis through a cell-type specific rewiring of cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous transcriptional programs
authors: Pereira MF; Finazzi V; Rizzuti L; Aprile D; Aiello V; Mollica L; Riva M; Soriani C; Dossena F; Shyti R; Castaldi D; Tenderini E; Carminho-Rodrigues MT; Bally JF; de Vries BB; Gabriele M; Vitriolo A; Testa G
one_liner_zh: 该文研究YY1突变通过细胞类型特异性转录网络重编程影响皮层发育，虽涉及转录因子YY1与基因调控网络，但核心是单细胞多组学与实验表型，缺乏TF-DNA结合位点预测、互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅部分相关。
abstract: Germline mutations of YY1 cause Gabriele-de Vries syndrome (GADEVS), a neurodevelopmental disorder featuring intellectual disability and a wide range of systemic manifestations. To dissect the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying GADEVS, we combined large-scale imaging, single-cell multiomics and gene regulatory network reconstruction in 2D and 3D patient-derived physiopathologically relevant cell lineages. YY1 haploinsufficiency causes a pervasive alteration of cell type specific transcriptional networks, disrupting corticogenesis at the level of neural progenitors and terminally differentiated neurons, including cytoarchitectural defects reminiscent of GADEVS clinical features. Transcriptional alterations in neurons propagated to neighboring astrocytes through a major non-cell autonomous pro-inflammatory effect that grounds the rationale for modulatory interventions. Together, neurodevelopmental trajectories, synaptic formation and neuronal-astrocyte cross talk emerged as salient domains of YY1 dosage-dependent vulnerability. Mechanistically, cell-type resolved reconstruction of gene regulatory networks uncovered the regulatory interplay between YY1, NEUROG2 and ETV5 and its aberrant rewiring in GADEVS. Our findings underscore the reach of advanced in vitro models in capturing developmental antecedents of clinical features and exposing their underlying mechanisms to guide the search for targeted interventions.
abstract_zh: YY1的胚系突变导致Gabriele-de Vries综合征（GADEVS），这是一种以智力障碍和多种全身性表现为特征的神经发育障碍。为解析GADEVS背后的细胞和分子机制，我们结合大规模成像、单细胞多组学及基因调控网络重建，在源自患者的2D和3D生理病理相关细胞谱系中进行了研究。YY1单倍剂量不足引起细胞类型特异性转录网络的广泛改变，在神经祖细胞和终末分化神经元水平上扰乱皮层生成，包括与GADEVS临床特征相似的细胞结构缺陷。神经元中的转录改变通过一种主要的非细胞自主促炎效应传播至邻近星形胶质细胞，这为调节性干预提供了理论基础。综合来看，神经发育轨迹、突触形成及神经元-星形胶质细胞串扰成为YY1剂量依赖性脆弱性的显著领域。机制上，细胞类型分辨的基因调控网络重建揭示了YY1、NEUROG2和ETV5之间的调控相互作用及其在GADEVS中的异常重连。我们的发现强调了先进体外模型在捕捉临床特征的发育前兆及揭示其潜在机制以指导靶向干预探索方面的重要性。
